Migdol (in Egypt)
MIG-dol
proper noun
Hebrew Migdol, “tower” or “watchtower”, from gadal, to be great; a frontier tower-city on the north-eastern border of Egypt, distinct from the Migdol of the Exodus encampment.

Biblical Definition

Migdol means “a tower”, and this Migdol was a fortress-town upon the north-eastern frontier of Egypt, a border watchtower where the fugitive remnant of Judah settled after they fled from the LORD’s appointed chastening. It is distinct from the Migdol of the Exodus, near which Israel encamped before the sea; this is the later frontier city where Jeremiah found the disobedient Jews: “The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the Jews which dwell in the land of Egypt, which dwell at Migdol, and at Tahpanhes, and at Noph, and in the country of Pathros” (Jer 44:1). They had gone down into Egypt against the plain command of God, thinking to hide behind Pharaoh’s towers from the sword and famine they feared; but the prophet declared that the sword they dreaded should overtake them there. Ezekiel marked the whole reach of Egypt’s coming desolation from that same border tower to the far south: the land should be made waste “from the tower of Syene even unto the border of Ethiopia” (Eze 29:10), which the margin reads “from Migdol to Syene”. From the northern watchtower to the southern cataract, the whole length of Egypt lay open to the judging hand of the LORD. Migdol teaches that no frontier fortress, no borrowed strength of the nations, can shelter the disobedient from God; His arm reaches from Migdol to Syene, and there is no border where He is not.

Webster 1828 Definition

A frontier tower-city on Egypt’s north-eastern border where fugitive Judah dwelt (Jer 44:1; Eze 29:10), distinct from the Exodus Migdol; a witness that no border escapes the LORD’s hand.

expand to see more

MIGDOL in Egypt, a tower-city on the north-eastern frontier (Jer 44:1).

Its name means “tower” or “watchtower”, a border fortress.

Distinct from the Migdol of the Exodus encampment by the sea.

The dwelling of Jews who fled to Egypt against God’s command.

“From Migdol to Syene”, the whole land lay under judgment (Eze 29:10).

Key Scripture

Jer 44:1 — "The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the Jews which dwell in the land of Egypt, which dwell at Migdol, and at Tahpanhes, and at Noph, and in the country of Pathros, saying,"

Eze 29:10 — "Behold, therefore I am against thee, and against thy rivers, and I will make the land of Egypt utterly waste and desolate, from the tower of Syene even unto the border of Ethiopia."

Jer 46:14 — "Declare ye in Egypt, and publish in Migdol, and publish in Noph and in Tahpanhes: say ye, Stand fast, and prepare thee; for the sword shall devour round about thee."

Isa 40:17 — "All nations before him are as nothing; and they are counted to him less than nothing, and vanity."

Modern Corruption

The frontier tower-city of Egypt where disobedient Judah sheltered; the entry recovers that no border fortress hides the disobedient from the reach of the LORD’s hand.

expand to see more

Migdol in Egypt is a border fortress named by the prophets, clearly distinct from the Migdol of the Exodus route; the tower-town itself raises no modern controversy, only the warning it carried to fugitive Judah.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that no frontier or borrowed strength can shelter the disobedient from God. Judah fled into Egypt against His plain word, thinking to hide behind Pharaoh’s towers from the sword and famine they feared, and settled at Migdol on the border; but the LORD declared the sword should find them there. From Migdol on the north to Syene in the far south the whole land lay open to His judging hand. The nations are less than nothing before Him, and there is no border where He is not.

Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Migdol, “tower, watchtower”, from gadal, to be great or grow, the same root as migdal, a tower.

expand to see more

Migdol — Hebrew Migdol, “tower, watchtower” (Jer 44:1).

From the root gadal, to be great, grow, or magnify.

Kindred to migdal, the common word for a tower.

This Migdol was a fortress upon Egypt’s north-eastern frontier.

Distinct from the Migdol of the Exodus by the sea (Exo 14:2).

Usage

"The fugitive Jews of Judah dwelt at Migdol on Egypt’s border."

"This Migdol is not the tower of the Exodus encampment."

"From Migdol to Syene the whole land of Egypt was judged."
